translations.literal: One star south of the Kitchen is called Celestial Record, governing the teeth of birds and beasts.
translations.idiomatic: One star south of the Kitchen is Celestial Record, governing beasts' teeth.

sentences.zh: 稷五星在七星南。

translations.literal: Millet has five stars south of Seven Stars.
translations.idiomatic: Millet has five stars south of Seven Stars.

sentences.zh: 稷，農正也。

translations.literal: Millet is the Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: Millet is the Minister of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 取乎百穀之長，以為號也。

translations.literal: It takes the longest of the hundred grains as its title.
translations.idiomatic: It takes the chief of grains as its name.

sentences.zh: 張南十四星曰天廟，天子之祖廟也。

translations.literal: Fourteen stars south of Extended Net are called Celestial Temple—the Son of Heaven's ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Fourteen stars south of Extended Net are Celestial Temple, the royal ancestral shrine.

sentences.zh: 客星守之，祠官有憂。

translations.literal: If a guest star guards it, sacrificial officers face grief.
translations.idiomatic: Guest stars guarding it bring grief to sacrificial officers.

sentences.zh: 翼南五星曰東區，蠻夷星也。

translations.literal: Five stars south of Wings are called Eastern Region—barbarian stars.
translations.idiomatic: Five stars south of Wings are Eastern Region—barbarian stars.

sentences.zh: 軫南三十二星曰器府，樂器之府也。

translations.literal: Thirty-two stars south of Chariot are called Instrument Storehouse—the storehouse of musical instruments.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty-two stars south of Chariot are Instrument Storehouse for musical instruments.

sentences.zh: 青丘七星在軫東南，蠻夷之國號也。

translations.literal: Green Mound has seven stars southeast of Chariot—the name of a barbarian state.
translations.idiomatic: Green Mound's seven stars southeast of Chariot mark a barbarian state.

sentences.zh: 青丘西四星曰土司空，主界域，亦曰司徒。

translations.literal: Four stars west of Green Mound are called Earth Minister, governing boundaries—also called Minister of Public Works.
translations.idiomatic: Four stars west of Green Mound are Earth Minister, governing boundaries.

sentences.zh: 土司空北二星曰軍門，主營候豹尾威旗。

translations.literal: Two stars north of Earth Minister are called Army Gate, governing camp watch, leopard tail, and battle flags.
translations.idiomatic: Two stars north of Earth Minister are Army Gate, governing camp watch and flags.

sentences.zh: 自攝提至此，大凡二百五十四官，一千二百八十三星。

translations.literal: From Sceptre Holder to here, in all two hundred fifty-four officials and one thousand two hundred eighty-three stars.
translations.idiomatic: From Sceptre Holder to here: two hundred fifty-four officials and one thousand two hundred eighty-three stars.

sentences.zh: 並二十八宿輔官，名曰經星常宿。

translations.literal: Together with the twenty-eight lodges' assisting officials, they are called the constant fixed stars.
translations.idiomatic: With the twenty-eight lodges' assistants, they are the constant fixed stars.

sentences.zh: 遠近有度，小大有差。

translations.literal: Near and far have their measures; small and large have their differences.
translations.idiomatic: Near and far have measure; large and small, difference.

sentences.zh: 苟或失常，實表災異。

translations.literal: If they ever lose normality, it truly signals disaster and anomaly.
translations.idiomatic: Abnormality truly signals disaster.

sentences.zh: 天漢，起東方，經尾箕之間，謂之漢津。

translations.literal: The Celestial River rises in the east, passing between Tail and Winnowing Basket—called the River Ford.
translations.idiomatic: The Celestial River rises east, passing Tail and Winnowing Basket—the River Ford.

sentences.zh: 乃分為二道，其南經傅說、魚、天籥、天弁、河鼓，其北經龜，貫箕下，次絡南斗魁、左旗，至天津下而合南道。

translations.literal: It then divides into two paths: the southern passes Fu Yue, Fish, Celestial Key, Celestial Cap, and River Drum; the northern passes Tortoise, pierces below Winnowing Basket, then links Southern Dipper head and Left Banner, reaching below Heavenly Ford and joining the southern path.
translations.idiomatic: It divides south through Fu Yue, Fish, and River Drum, and north through Tortoise and Southern Dipper, joining at Heavenly Ford.

sentences.zh: 乃西南行，又分夾匏瓜，絡人星、杵、造父、騰蛇、王良、傅路、閣道北端、太陵、天船、捲舌而南行，絡五車，經北河之南，入東井水位而東南行，絡南河、闕丘、天狗、天紀、天稷，在七星南而沒。

translations.literal: It then travels southwest, again divides to flank Gourd, links Human Star, Pestle, Zao Fu, Coiled Snake, Wang Liang, Fu Road, north end of Level Road, Great Mound, Celestial Ship, Rolled Tongue southward, links Five Chariots, passes south of North River, enters Eastern Well Water Level southeast, links South River, Gate Mound, Celestial Dog, Celestial Record, Celestial Millet south of Seven Stars, and sets.
translations.idiomatic: Then southwest through Gourd, Five Chariots, Eastern Well, and Seven Stars, where it sets.

sentences.zh: 天占《鴻範五行傳》曰：「清而明者，天之體也，天忽變色，是謂易常。

translations.literal: Heaven's divination, the Hong Fan Wuxing Commentary says: "Clear and bright is Heaven's body; if Heaven suddenly changes color, this is called altering the constant."
translations.idiomatic: The Hong Fan Wuxing Commentary says: "Clear and bright is Heaven's body; sudden color change alters the constant."

sentences.zh: 天裂，陽不足，是謂臣強，下將害上，國後分裂，其下之主當之。

translations.literal: Heaven splits—yang is insufficient, meaning ministers are strong, subordinates will harm superiors, the state later splits, and the lord below will suffer for it.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven splits means insufficient yang—strong ministers, split realm, suffering lords.

sentences.zh: 天開見光，流血滂滂。

translations.literal: Heaven opens and light appears—blood flows in torrents.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven opening to light brings torrents of blood.

sentences.zh: 天裂見人，兵起國亡。

translations.literal: Heaven splits and people are seen—armies rise and the state perishes.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven splitting with visible people means war and national ruin.

sentences.zh: 天鳴有聲，至尊憂且驚。

translations.literal: Heaven sounds with noise—the Supreme One grieves and is startled.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's sound means the Supreme One grieves and startles.

sentences.zh: 皆亂國之所生也。

translations.literal: All are born of a disordered state.
translations.idiomatic: All arise from a disordered state.

sentences.zh: 漢惠帝二年，天開東北，長三十餘丈，廣十餘丈。

translations.literal: In Han Emperor Hui's second year, Heaven opened in the northeast, thirty-plus zhang long and ten-plus zhang wide.
translations.idiomatic: In Han Hui's second year, Heaven opened northeast—thirty-plus zhang long.

sentences.zh: 後有呂氏變亂。

translations.literal: Afterward came the Lü clan's rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward came the Lü clan rebellion.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝太安二年，天中裂。

translations.literal: In Jin Emperor Hui's Tai'an second year, Heaven split at the center.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin Hui's Tai'an second year, Heaven split at center.

sentences.zh: 穆帝升平五年，又裂，廣數丈，並有聲如雷。

translations.literal: Emperor Mu's Shengping fifth year, it split again, several zhang wide, and there was sound like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: Mu Di's Shengping fifth year: another split, several zhang wide, with thunder.

sentences.zh: 其後皆有兵革之應。

translations.literal: Afterward all had responses of warfare.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward all brought warfare.

sentences.zh: 七曜日循黃道東行，一日一夜行一度，三百六十五日有奇而周天。

translations.literal: The seven luminaries: the sun follows the Yellow Path eastward, traveling one degree in one day and night, completing a circuit in three hundred sixty-five and a fraction days.
translations.idiomatic: The sun follows the ecliptic eastward one degree per day, circling in 365+ days.

sentences.zh: 行東陸謂之春，行南陸謂之夏，行西陸謂之秋，行北陸謂之冬。

translations.literal: Traveling the eastern quarter is called spring; southern, summer; western, autumn; northern, winter.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern travel is spring; southern, summer; western, autumn; northern, winter.

sentences.zh: 行以成陰陽寒暑之節。

translations.literal: Its travel completes the nodes of yin-yang, cold and heat.
translations.idiomatic: Its travel sets the nodes of yin-yang and seasons.

sentences.zh: 是故《傳》云：「日為太陽之精，主生養恩德，人君之象也。

translations.literal: Therefore the Commentary says: "The sun is the essence of Great Yang, governing nurturing virtue and grace, the image of the human lord."
translations.idiomatic: The Commentary says: "The sun is Great Yang's essence, the image of the human lord."

sentences.zh: 」又人君有瑕，必露其慝，以告示焉。

translations.literal: Also, when the human lord has flaws, his wickedness must be exposed to give warning.
translations.idiomatic: When the ruler has flaws, his wickedness is exposed as warning.

sentences.zh: 故日月行有道之國則光明，人君吉昌，百姓安寧。

translations.literal: Therefore when sun and moon travel through a state with the Way, they are bright, the lord is auspicious, and the people are at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Sun and moon in a righteous state shine bright—the lord prospers and people are at peace.

sentences.zh: 日變色，有軍軍破，無軍喪侯王。

translations.literal: If the sun changes color, with armies they are destroyed; without armies, marquises and kings mourn.
translations.idiomatic: Sun color change destroys armies—or mourns lords without armies.

sentences.zh: 其君無德，其臣亂國，則日赤無光。

translations.literal: If the lord lacks virtue and ministers disorder the state, the sun is red without light.
translations.idiomatic: A virtueless lord and disorderly ministers make the sun red and dim.

sentences.zh: 日失色，所臨之國不昌。

translations.literal: If the sun loses color, the state it faces does not flourish.
translations.idiomatic: A discolored sun means the state it faces fails.

sentences.zh: 日晝昏，行人無影，到暮不止者，上刑急，下人不聊生，不出一年，有大水。

translations.literal: If the sun is dim at midday, travelers cast no shadow until evening without stopping, punishments above are harsh, people below cannot live—in less than a year, great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Midday dim sun with no shadows means harsh punishments and great flood within a year.

sentences.zh: 日晝昏，烏鳥群鳴，國失政。

translations.literal: If the sun is dim at day and crows flock, government is lost.
translations.idiomatic: Daytime dim sun with flocking crows means lost government.

sentences.zh: 日中烏見，主不明，為政亂，國有白衣會。

translations.literal: If a crow appears in the sun, the lord is not enlightened, government is chaotic, and the state has a white-clad assembly.
translations.idiomatic: A crow in the sun means a darkened lord, chaotic rule, and white-clad assembly.

sentences.zh: 日中有黑子、黑氣、黑雲，乍三乍五，臣廢其主。

translations.literal: Black spots, black qi, or black clouds in the sun, appearing three or five at a time—ministers depose their lord.
translations.idiomatic: Black spots, qi, or clouds in the sun mean ministers depose their lord.

sentences.zh: 日食，陰侵陽，臣掩君之象，有亡國，有死君，有大水。

translations.literal: Solar eclipse: yin invades yang, ministers cover the lord—there is a fallen state, a dead lord, or great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Solar eclipse: yin invades yang—fallen states, dead lords, or great floods.

sentences.zh: 日食見星，有殺君，天下分裂。

translations.literal: If stars are seen during solar eclipse, a lord is killed and the realm splits.
translations.idiomatic: Stars visible during eclipse mean a killed lord and a split realm.

sentences.zh: 王者修德以禳之。

translations.literal: Kings cultivate virtue to avert it.
translations.idiomatic: Kings cultivate virtue to avert it.

sentences.zh: 月者，陰之精也。

translations.literal: The moon is the essence of yin.
translations.idiomatic: The moon is yin's essence.

sentences.zh: 其形圓，其質清，日光照之，則見其明。

translations.literal: Its form is round, its substance clear; when sunlight shines on it, its brightness is seen.
translations.idiomatic: Round and clear, it shows brightness when sunlight strikes it.

sentences.zh: 日光所不照，則謂之魄。

translations.literal: Where sunlight does not shine is called the dark portion.
translations.idiomatic: Where sunlight does not reach is the dark portion.

sentences.zh: 故月望之日，日月相望，人居其間，盡睹其明，故形圓也。

translations.literal: Thus on the full-moon day, sun and moon face each other; people stand between them and see all its brightness—therefore the form is round.
translations.idiomatic: At full moon, sun and moon face each other; people between see a round disk.

sentences.zh: 二弦之日，日照其側，人觀其傍，故半明半魄也。

translations.literal: On the two quarter days, sunlight strikes the side and people view from the side—therefore half bright and half dark.
translations.idiomatic: At quarter moons, sunlight strikes the side—half bright, half dark.

sentences.zh: 晦朔之日，日照其表，人在其裡，故不見也。

translations.literal: On new and full moon days, sunlight strikes the face and people are within—therefore it is not seen.
translations.idiomatic: At new and full moon, sunlight strikes the face and the moon is not seen.

sentences.zh: 其行有遲疾。

translations.literal: Its travel has slow and fast phases.
translations.idiomatic: Its motion has slow and fast phases.

sentences.zh: 其極遲則日行十二度強，極疾則日行十四度半強。

translations.literal: At greatest slowness the sun travels twelve and a fraction degrees per day; at greatest speed, fourteen and a half degrees.
translations.idiomatic: At slowest the sun moves twelve+ degrees daily; at fastest, fourteen and a half.

sentences.zh: 遲則漸疾，疾極漸遲，二十七日半強而遲疾一終矣。

translations.literal: Slow gradually becomes fast; at greatest speed gradually becomes slow—twenty-seven and a half days complete one slow-fast cycle.
translations.idiomatic: Slow turns fast, fast turns slow—a full cycle in twenty-seven and a half days.

sentences.zh: 又月行之道，斜帶黃道。

translations.literal: Also the moon's path slants across the Yellow Path.
translations.idiomatic: The moon's path slants across the ecliptic.

sentences.zh: 十三日有奇在黃道表，又十三日有奇在黃道裡。

translations.literal: Thirteen and a fraction days north of the ecliptic, then thirteen and a fraction south.
translations.idiomatic: Thirteen+ days north of the ecliptic, then thirteen+ south.

sentences.zh: 表裡極遠者，去黃道六度。

translations.literal: At greatest north-south distance, six degrees from the ecliptic.
translations.idiomatic: Maximum deviation from the ecliptic is six degrees.

sentences.zh: 二十七日有奇，陰陽一終。

translations.literal: Twenty-seven and a fraction days complete one yin-yang cycle.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-seven+ days complete one yin-yang cycle.

sentences.zh: 張衡云：「對日之衝，其大如日，日光不照，謂之暗虛。

translations.literal: Zhang Heng said: "Facing the sun's opposite point, it is as large as the sun; sunlight does not shine there—this is called the dark void."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Heng: "Opposite the sun lies the dark void where sunlight does not reach."

sentences.zh: 暗虛逢月則月食，值星則星亡。

translations.literal: When the dark void meets the moon, lunar eclipse; when it meets a star, the star vanishes."
translations.idiomatic: Dark void meeting moon causes eclipse; meeting a star, the star vanishes."

sentences.zh: 」今曆家月望行黃道，則值暗虛矣。

translations.literal: Calendrical masters now have the full moon travel the Yellow Path—then it meets the dark void.
translations.idiomatic: Modern calendars place full moon on the ecliptic—meeting the dark void.

sentences.zh: 值暗虛有表裡深淺，故食有南北多少。

translations.literal: Meeting the dark void has inner and outer depth—therefore eclipses differ north-south and in amount.
translations.idiomatic: Dark void depth varies—so eclipses differ in depth and direction.

sentences.zh: 月為太陰之精，以之配日，女主之象也。

translations.literal: The moon is the essence of Great Yin, paired with the sun—the image of the queen consort.
translations.idiomatic: The moon is Great Yin's essence, paired with the sun—the queen's image.

sentences.zh: 以之比德，刑罰之義。

translations.literal: Compared to virtue, it is the meaning of punishment.
translations.idiomatic: In virtue it represents punishment.

sentences.zh: 列之朝廷，諸侯大臣之類。

translations.literal: Arrayed at court, it is the class of feudal lords and great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: At court it images feudal lords and great ministers.

sentences.zh: 故君明則月行依度，臣執權則月行失道。

translations.literal: Therefore if the lord is enlightened the moon travels by measure; if ministers hold power the moon loses its path.
translations.idiomatic: An enlightened lord keeps the moon on course; powerful ministers make it stray.

sentences.zh: 大臣用事，兵刑失理，則月行乍南乍北。

translations.literal: If great ministers hold affairs and military punishment is unjust, the moon suddenly goes south then north.
translations.idiomatic: Ministerial power and unjust punishment make the moon shift south and north.

sentences.zh: 女主外戚擅權，則或進或退。

translations.literal: If the queen consort and maternal kin usurp power, it advances or retreats.
translations.idiomatic: Queen consort and kin usurping power make it advance or retreat.

sentences.zh: 月變色，將有殃。

translations.literal: If the moon changes color, calamity will come.
translations.idiomatic: Moon color change foretells calamity.

sentences.zh: 月晝明，奸邪並作，君臣爭明，女主失行，陰國兵強，中國饑，天下謀僭。

translations.literal: If the moon is bright by day, wickedness rises together, lord and ministers contend for light, the queen consort misbehaves, yin states grow strong in arms, the central realm hungers, the realm plots usurpation.
translations.idiomatic: Day-bright moon brings wickedness, ministerial rivalry, queen's misconduct, border strength, central famine, and usurpation.

sentences.zh: 數月重見，國以亂亡。

translations.literal: If seen repeatedly for months, the state falls to chaos and perishes.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated monthly appearances mean chaos and ruin.

sentences.zh: 歲星曰東方春木。

translations.literal: The Year Star is Eastern spring wood.
translations.idiomatic: The Year Star is eastern spring wood.

sentences.zh: 于人五常，仁也；

translations.literal: Among the five constants of humanity, benevolence;
translations.idiomatic: Among humanity's five constants: benevolence;

sentences.zh: 五事，貌也。

translations.literal: among the five affairs, appearance.
translations.idiomatic: among the five affairs: appearance.

sentences.zh: 仁虧貌失，逆春令，傷木氣，則罰見歲星。

translations.literal: If benevolence fails and appearance is lost, violating spring command and injuring wood qi—the punishment appears in the Year Star.
translations.idiomatic: Failed benevolence and appearance, violating spring and injuring wood qi—punishment shows in the Year Star.

sentences.zh: 歲星盈縮，以其捨命國。

translations.literal: The Year Star's expansion and contraction—take omens from the state where it lodges.
translations.idiomatic: Read omens from the state the Year Star lodges in.

sentences.zh: 其所居久，其國有德厚，五穀豐昌，不可伐。

translations.literal: Where it dwells long, that state has thick virtue, abundant grain, and cannot be attacked.
translations.idiomatic: Long dwelling means thick virtue, abundant grain, and invulnerability.

sentences.zh: 其對為衝，歲乃有殃。

translations.literal: Its opposite is opposition—the Year Star then brings calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Opposition brings Year Star calamity.

sentences.zh: 歲星安靜中度，吉。

translations.literal: If the Year Star is quiet at mid-degree, auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: A quiet Year Star at mid-degree is auspicious.

sentences.zh: 盈縮失次，其國有變，不可舉事用兵。

translations.literal: Expansion, contraction, or losing position—that state changes; do not raise armies or undertake affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Expansion, contraction, or lost position means change—do not make war.

sentences.zh: 又曰，人主出象也。

translations.literal: It is also said: the image of the human lord.
translations.idiomatic: Also: the image of the human lord.

sentences.zh: 色欲明光潤澤，德合同。

translations.literal: Its color should be bright, lustrous, and moist—virtue and harmony agree.
translations.idiomatic: Color should be bright, lustrous, moist—virtue in harmony.

sentences.zh: 又曰，進退如度，奸邪息；

translations.literal: Also: advancing and retreating by measure, wickedness ceases;
translations.idiomatic: Also: motion by measure ends wickedness;

sentences.zh: 變色亂行，主無福。

translations.literal: changing color and disorderly travel—the lord has no fortune.
translations.idiomatic: color change and disorderly motion—the lord lacks fortune.

sentences.zh: 又主福，主大司農，主齊、吳，主司天下諸侯人君之過，主歲五穀。

translations.literal: Also governing fortune, the Grand Minister of Agriculture, Qi and Wu, all feudal lords' and lords' faults under Heaven, and the year's five grains.
translations.idiomatic: Also fortune, Grand Minister of Agriculture, Qi and Wu, lords' faults, and yearly grain.

sentences.zh: 赤而角，其國昌；

translations.literal: Red with horns—that state flourishes;
translations.idiomatic: Red with horns: that state flourishes;

sentences.zh: 赤黃而沉，其野大穰。

translations.literal: red-yellow and sunken—the fields greatly abundant.
translations.idiomatic: red-yellow and sunken: great harvest.

sentences.zh: 熒惑曰南方夏火。

translations.literal: Sparkling Fire is southern summer fire.
translations.idiomatic: Sparkling Fire is southern summer fire.

sentences.zh: 禮也，視也。

translations.literal: Ritual and vision.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual and vision.

sentences.zh: 禮虧視失，逆夏令，傷火氣，罰見熒惑。

translations.literal: Failed ritual and vision, violating summer command and injuring fire qi—the punishment appears in Sparkling Fire.
translations.idiomatic: Failed ritual and vision, violating summer—punishment in Sparkling Fire.

sentences.zh: 熒惑法使行無常，出則有兵，入則兵散。

translations.literal: Sparkling Fire's law makes travel without constancy; when it emerges there is war, when it enters armies scatter.
translations.idiomatic: Sparkling Fire travels without constancy—emergence brings war, entry scatters armies.

sentences.zh: 以捨命國，為亂，為賊，為疾，為喪，為饑，為兵，居國受殃。

translations.literal: Take omens from the lodging state—chaos, banditry, disease, mourning, famine, war; the state where it lodges suffers calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Lodging brings chaos, banditry, disease, mourning, famine, war.

sentences.zh: 環繞勾已，芒角動搖變色，乍前乍後，乍左乍右，其殃愈甚。

translations.literal: Circling, hooking, horned rays trembling and changing color, now forward now back, now left now right—the calamity grows worse.
translations.idiomatic: Circling, hooks, trembling horns, shifting color and direction—calamity worsens.

sentences.zh: 其南丈夫、北女子喪。

translations.literal: To its south, husbands mourn; to its north, women mourn.
translations.idiomatic: South: husbands mourn; north: women mourn.

sentences.zh: 周旋止息，乃為死喪，寇亂其野，亡地。

translations.literal: Circling, stopping, and resting then become death and mourning; bandits ravage the wilds and land is lost.
translations.idiomatic: Circling and stopping become death; bandits ravage and land is lost.

sentences.zh: 其失行而速，兵聚其下，順之戰勝。

translations.literal: If it loses its path and is fast, armies gather below; following it, battle is victorious.
translations.idiomatic: Fast and off-path, armies gather below; following it wins battle.

sentences.zh: 又曰，熒惑主大鴻臚，主死喪，主司空，又為司馬，主楚、吳、越以南，又司天下群臣之過，司驕奢亡亂妖孽，主歲成敗。

translations.literal: Also: Sparkling Fire governs the Grand Herald, death and mourning, Minister of Works, also Marshal, Chu-Wu-Yue south, all ministers' faults, arrogance, chaos, and wicked omens, and the year's success and failure.
translations.idiomatic: Also: Herald, mourning, Works, Marshal, south, ministers' faults, and yearly fortune.

sentences.zh: 又曰，熒惑不動，兵不戰，有誅將。

translations.literal: Also: if Sparkling Fire does not move, no battle—but a general is executed.
translations.idiomatic: Also: unmoving Sparkling Fire means no battle but a executed general.

sentences.zh: 其出色赤怒，逆行成鉤已，戰凶，有圍軍。

translations.literal: Emerging red and angry, retrograde forming hooks—battle is inauspicious, armies besieged.
translations.idiomatic: Red angry emergence with retrograde hooks—inauspicious battle and siege.

sentences.zh: 鉤已，有芒角如鋒刃，人主無出宮，下有伏兵。

translations.literal: Hooks with horned rays like blades—the lord must not leave the palace; ambush below.
translations.idiomatic: Hooked horned rays like blades—the lord stays in palace; ambush below.

sentences.zh: 芒大則人民怒，君子遑遑，小人浪浪，不有亂臣，則有大喪，人欺吏，吏欺王。

translations.literal: Large horns—people rage; gentlemen restless, petty men unrestrained; if no rebellious ministers, great mourning; officials deceive clerks, clerks deceive the king.
translations.idiomatic: Large horns: popular rage, restless gentlemen, unrestrained petty men, rebellion or great mourning, official deceit.

sentences.zh: 又為外則兵，內則理政，為天子之理也。

translations.literal: Also external means war, internal means governing—this is the Son of Heaven's principle.
translations.idiomatic: External: war; internal: governance—the Son of Heaven's principle.

sentences.zh: 故曰，雖有明天子，必視熒惑所在。

translations.literal: Therefore even with a bright Son of Heaven, one must observe where Sparkling Fire lodges.
translations.idiomatic: Even a bright Son of Heaven must watch Sparkling Fire's place.

sentences.zh: 其入守犯太微、軒轅、營室、房、心，主命惡之。

translations.literal: If it enters and guards Supreme Subtlety, Chariot Pivot, Encampment, Chamber, or Heart—the lord's mandate is hated.
translations.idiomatic: Entering Supreme Subtlety, Chariot Pivot, Encampment, Chamber, or Heart—the mandate is hated.

sentences.zh: 填星曰中央季夏土。

translations.literal: Fill Star is central late-summer earth.
translations.idiomatic: Fill Star is central late-summer earth.

sentences.zh: 信也，思心也。

translations.literal: Faith and the thinking heart.
translations.idiomatic: Faith and the thinking heart.

sentences.zh: 仁義禮智，以信為主，貌言視聽，以心為政，故四星皆失，填乃為之動。

translations.literal: Benevolence, righteousness, ritual, wisdom—with faith as master; appearance, speech, vision, hearing—with the heart as government—therefore when all four stars fail, Fill moves for them.
translations.idiomatic: When benevolence, ritual, wisdom fail, Fill Star moves.

sentences.zh: 動而盈，侯王不寧。

translations.literal: Moving and expanding—marquises and kings are unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: Moving and expanding unsettles marquises and kings.

sentences.zh: 縮，有軍不復。

translations.literal: Contracting—armies do not return.
translations.idiomatic: Contracting: armies do not return.

sentences.zh: 所居之宿，國吉，得地及女子，有福，不可伐。

translations.literal: The lodge where it dwells—the state is auspicious, gains land and women, has fortune, cannot be attacked.
translations.idiomatic: Its lodge: auspicious state, land and women, fortune, invulnerable.

sentences.zh: 去之，失地，若有女憂。

translations.literal: Departing—land is lost; if women grieve.
translations.idiomatic: Departing: lost land and grieving women.

sentences.zh: 居宿久，國福厚，易則薄。

translations.literal: Dwelling long—the state's fortune is thick; changing, thin.
translations.idiomatic: Long dwelling: thick fortune; changing: thin.

sentences.zh: 失次而上二三宿曰盈，有主命不成，不乃大水。

translations.literal: Losing position upward two or three lodges is called expanding—the lord's mandate unfulfilled, or great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Expanding upward two-three lodges: unfulfilled mandate or great flood.

sentences.zh: 失次而下曰縮，後戚，其歲不復，不乃天裂，若地動。

translations.literal: Losing position downward is called contracting—rear kin, the year does not recover, or Heaven splits, or earth quakes.
translations.idiomatic: Contracting downward: rear kin, failed harvest, Heaven splits, or earthquake.

sentences.zh: 一曰，填為黃帝之德，女主之象，主德厚，安危存亡之機，司天下女主之過。

translations.literal: One says: Fill is Yellow Emperor's virtue, the queen consort's image, governing thick virtue, the pivot of safety and peril, overseeing all queen consorts' faults under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Fill is Yellow Emperor's virtue and the queen's image, governing safety and queens' faults.

sentences.zh: 又曰，天子之星也。

translations.literal: Also: the Son of Heaven's star.
translations.idiomatic: Also: the Son of Heaven's star.

sentences.zh: 天子失信，則填星大動。

translations.literal: If the Son of Heaven loses faith, Fill Star moves greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Lost faith makes Fill Star move greatly.

sentences.zh: 太白曰西方秋金。

translations.literal: Great White is western autumn metal.
translations.idiomatic: Great White is western autumn metal.

sentences.zh: 義也，言也。

translations.literal: Righteousness and speech.
translations.idiomatic: Righteousness and speech.

sentences.zh: 義虧言失，逆秋令，傷金氣，罰見太白。

translations.literal: Failed righteousness and speech, violating autumn and injuring metal qi—punishment appears in Great White.
translations.idiomatic: Failed righteousness and speech, violating autumn—punishment in Great White.

sentences.zh: 太白進退以候兵，高埤遲速，靜躁見伏，用兵皆象之，吉。

translations.literal: Great White's advance and retreat watch for armies; high and low, slow and fast, quiet and restless, visibility and hiding—all image military use; auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Great White's motion images armies—auspicious when orderly.

sentences.zh: 其出西方，失行，夷狄敗；

translations.literal: Emerging west and losing path—barbarians are defeated;
translations.idiomatic: West emergence off-path: barbarians defeated;

sentences.zh: 出東方，失行，中國敗。

translations.literal: emerging east and losing path—the central realm is defeated.
translations.idiomatic: east emergence off-path: central realm defeated.

sentences.zh: 未盡期日，過參天，病其對國。

translations.literal: Before the term ends, passing mid-heaven—illness to the opposite state.
translations.idiomatic: Before term ends, passing mid-heaven: illness to opposite state.

sentences.zh: 若經天，天下革，人更王，是謂亂紀，人民流亡。

translations.literal: If it crosses heaven, the realm is transformed, people change kings—this is called disordering the order; people wander in exile.
translations.idiomatic: Crossing heaven transforms the realm, changes kings, exiles people.

sentences.zh: 晝與日爭明，強國弱，小國強，女主昌。

translations.literal: Contending brightness with the sun by day—strong states weaken, small states strengthen, the queen consort flourishes.
translations.idiomatic: Daytime brightness rivalry: strong weaken, small strengthen, queen flourishes.

sentences.zh: 又曰，太白大臣，其號上公也，大司馬位謹候此。

translations.literal: Also: Great White is a great minister, titled Supreme Duke; the Grand Marshal's seat carefully watches this.
translations.idiomatic: Great White is Supreme Duke; the Grand Marshal watches it.

sentences.zh: 辰星曰北方冬水。

translations.literal: Chronogram Star is northern winter water.
translations.idiomatic: Chronogram Star is northern winter water.

sentences.zh: 智也，聽也。

translations.literal: Wisdom and hearing.
translations.idiomatic: Wisdom and hearing.

sentences.zh: 智虧聽失，逆冬令，傷水氣，罰見辰星。

translations.literal: Failed wisdom and hearing, violating winter and injuring water qi—punishment appears in Chronogram Star.
translations.idiomatic: Failed wisdom and hearing, violating winter—punishment in Chronogram Star.

sentences.zh: 辰星見，主刑，主廷尉，主燕、趙，又為燕、趙、代以北，宰相之象，亦為殺伐之氣，戰鬭之象。

translations.literal: When Chronogram Star appears, it governs punishment, the Minister of Justice, Yan and Zhao, also Yan-Zhao-Dai north, the chancellor's image, also killing qi and the image of battle.
translations.idiomatic: Chronogram Star governs punishment, justice, Yan-Zhao, and battle.

sentences.zh: 又曰，軍於野，辰星為偏將之象，無軍為刑事。

translations.literal: Also: armies in the field—Chronogram Star is the flank general's image; without armies, criminal affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In field: flank general; without armies: criminal affairs.

sentences.zh: 和陰陽，應其時。

translations.literal: Harmonizing yin and yang, responding to the season.
translations.idiomatic: Harmonizing yin-yang, responding to season.

sentences.zh: 不和，出失其時，寒暑失其節，邦當大饑。

translations.literal: Not harmonizing, emerging at wrong season—cold and heat lose their nodes; the state faces great famine.
translations.idiomatic: Disharmony and wrong-season emergence bring great famine.

sentences.zh: 當出不出，是謂擊卒，兵大起。

translations.literal: Should emerge but does not—this is called striking soldiers; armies rise greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Failure to emerge means striking soldiers and great armies.

sentences.zh: 在於房心間，地動。

translations.literal: Between Chamber and Heart—earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: Between Chamber and Heart: earthquake.

sentences.zh: 亦曰，辰星出入躁疾，常主夷狄。

translations.literal: Also: Chronogram Star's emergence is restless and fast, regularly governing barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Also: fast restless emergence governs barbarians.

sentences.zh: 又曰，蠻夷出星，亦主刑法之得失。

translations.literal: Also: barbarian stars emerging also govern gain and loss in criminal law.
translations.idiomatic: Also: barbarian stars govern criminal law.

sentences.zh: 色黃而小，地大動。

translations.literal: Yellow and small color—great earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow small color: great earthquake.

sentences.zh: 凡五星有色，大小不同，各依其行而順時應節。

translations.literal: Generally the five planets have color; large and small differ, each following its nature and responding to season and node.
translations.idiomatic: Five planets differ in color and size, each following its nature and season.

sentences.zh: 色變有類。

translations.literal: Color change has categories.
translations.idiomatic: Color change has categories.

sentences.zh: 凡青皆比參左肩，赤比心大星，黃比參右肩，白比狼星，黑比奎大星。

translations.literal: All green compares to Three Stars' left shoulder; red to Heart's great star; yellow to Three Stars' right shoulder; white to Wolf Star; black to Strider's great star.
translations.idiomatic: Green like left shoulder; red like Heart; yellow like right shoulder; white like Wolf; black like Strider.

sentences.zh: 不失本色，而應其四時者，吉；

translations.literal: Not losing native color and responding to the four seasons—auspicious;
translations.idiomatic: Keeping native color through four seasons is auspicious;

sentences.zh: 色害其行，凶。

translations.literal: color harming its nature—in auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: color harming its nature is inauspicious.

sentences.zh: 凡五星所出所行所直之辰，其國為得位者，歲星以德，熒惑有禮，填星有福，太白兵強，辰星陰陽和。

translations.literal: Generally at the chronogram where the five planets emerge, travel, and stand upright, the state gains position: Year Star by virtue, Sparkling Fire by ritual, Fill Star by fortune, Great White by strong armies, Chronogram Star by yin-yang harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Lodging states gain: Year by virtue, Fire by ritual, Fill by fortune, White by armies, Chronogram by harmony.

sentences.zh: 所行所直之辰，順其色而有角者勝，其色害者敗。

translations.literal: At the chronogram of emergence, travel, and upright stance—following its color with horns means victory; color harmed means defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Color with horns at lodging wins; harmed color loses.

sentences.zh: 居實，有德也。

translations.literal: Dwelling in fullness—has virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Dwelling in fullness: virtue.

sentences.zh: 居虛，無德也。

translations.literal: Dwelling in emptiness—no virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Dwelling in emptiness: no virtue.

sentences.zh: 色勝位，行勝色，行得盡勝之。

translations.literal: Color conquers position, motion conquers color, motion attaining all conquers completely.
translations.idiomatic: Color beats position, motion beats color, full conquest wins all.

sentences.zh: 營室為清廟，歲星廟也。

translations.literal: Encampment is the Pure Temple—Year Star's temple.
translations.idiomatic: Encampment is Pure Temple—Year Star's temple.

sentences.zh: 心為明堂，熒惑廟也。

translations.literal: Heart is the Bright Hall—Sparkling Fire's temple.
translations.idiomatic: Heart is Bright Hall—Sparkling Fire's temple.

sentences.zh: 南斗為文太室，填星廟也。

translations.literal: Southern Dipper is the Literary Grand Chamber—Fill Star's temple.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Dipper is Literary Grand Chamber—Fill Star's temple.

sentences.zh: 亢為疏廟，太白廟也。

translations.literal: Neck is the Dispersal Temple—Great White's temple.
translations.idiomatic: Neck is Dispersal Temple—Great White's temple.

sentences.zh: 七星為員官，辰星廟也。

translations.literal: Seven Stars is the Round Office—Chronogram Star's temple.
translations.idiomatic: Seven Stars is Round Office—Chronogram Star's temple.

sentences.zh: 五星行至其廟，謹候其命。

translations.literal: When the five planets reach their temples, carefully await their commands.
translations.idiomatic: At their temples, carefully await the five planets' commands.

sentences.zh: 凡五星盈縮失位，其精降于地為人。

translations.literal: Generally when the five planets expand, contract, or lose position, their essences descend to earth as humans.
translations.idiomatic: When five planets expand, contract, or lose position, their essences descend as humans.

sentences.zh: 歲星降為貴臣；

translations.literal: Year Star descending becomes a noble minister;
translations.idiomatic: Year Star descending becomes a noble minister;

sentences.zh: 熒惑降為童兒，歌謠嬉戲；

translations.literal: Sparkling Fire descending becomes children, songs, and playful games;
translations.idiomatic: Sparkling Fire descending becomes singing children;

sentences.zh: 填星降為老人婦女；

translations.literal: Fill Star descending becomes old men and women;
translations.idiomatic: Fill Star descending becomes old men and women;

sentences.zh: 太白降為壯夫，處於林麓；

translations.literal: Great White descending becomes strong men dwelling in forest foothills;
translations.idiomatic: Great White descending becomes strong men in forests;

sentences.zh: 辰星降為婦人。

translations.literal: Chronogram Star descending becomes women.
translations.idiomatic: Chronogram Star descending becomes women.

sentences.zh: 吉凶之應，隨其象告。

translations.literal: Responses of fortune and misfortune follow their images in announcement.
translations.idiomatic: Fortune and misfortune follow their announced images.

sentences.zh: 凡五星，木與土合，為內亂、饑；

translations.literal: Generally among the five planets: wood meeting earth—internal chaos and famine;
translations.idiomatic: Wood meeting earth: internal chaos and famine;

sentences.zh: 與水合，為變謀而更事；

translations.literal: meeting water—changed plots and changed affairs;
translations.idiomatic: meeting water: changed plots and affairs;

sentences.zh: 與火合，為饑，為旱；

translations.literal: meeting fire—famine and drought;
translations.idiomatic: meeting fire: famine and drought;

sentences.zh: 與金合，為白衣之會；

translations.literal: meeting metal—white-clad assembly;
translations.idiomatic: meeting metal: white-clad assembly;

sentences.zh: 合鬭，國有內亂，野有破軍，為水。

translations.literal: combining in battle—internal chaos in the state, broken armies in the wild, water.
translations.idiomatic: Battle combination: internal chaos, broken armies, flood.

sentences.zh: 太白在南，歲星在北，名曰牡年，穀大熟。

translations.literal: Great White in the south, Year Star in the north—called a male year; grain greatly ripens.
translations.idiomatic: Great White south, Year Star north—a male year, great harvest.

sentences.zh: 太白在北，歲星在南，年或有或無。

translations.literal: Great White in the north, Year Star in the south—the year may or may not have grain.
translations.idiomatic: Great White north, Year Star south—grain uncertain.

sentences.zh: 火與金合，為爍為喪，不可舉事用兵。

translations.literal: Fire meeting metal—blazing and mourning; do not raise armies or undertake affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Fire meeting metal: blazing and mourning—no war.

sentences.zh: 從軍為軍憂，離之軍卻。

translations.literal: Following armies brings army grief; departing armies retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Following armies grieves them; departing armies retreat.

sentences.zh: 出太白陰，分宅，出其陽，偏將戰。

translations.literal: Emerging from Great White's yin—partition of estates; from its yang—flank generals battle.
translations.idiomatic: From White's yin: partition; from yang: flank battle.

sentences.zh: 與土合，為憂，主孽。

translations.literal: Meeting earth—grief, lord's wicked offspring.
translations.idiomatic: Meeting earth: grief and wicked offspring.

sentences.zh: 與水合，為北軍，用兵舉事大敗。

translations.literal: Meeting water—northern armies; raising armies and affairs greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Meeting water: northern armies and great defeat.

sentences.zh: 一曰，火與水合為焠，不可舉事用兵。

translations.literal: One says: fire meeting water is quenching; do not raise armies.
translations.idiomatic: Also: fire and water quench—no war.

sentences.zh: 土與水合，為壅沮，不可舉事用兵，有覆軍下師。

translations.literal: Earth meeting water—obstruction; do not raise armies; overturned armies and defeated generals below.
translations.idiomatic: Earth and water obstruct—defeated armies below.

sentences.zh: 一曰，為變謀更事，必為旱。

translations.literal: One says: changed plots and changed affairs; certainly drought.
translations.idiomatic: Also: changed plots—certain drought.

sentences.zh: 與金合，為疾，為白衣會，為內兵，國亡地。

translations.literal: Meeting metal—disease, white-clad assembly, internal armies, state lost land.
translations.idiomatic: Meeting metal: disease, white assembly, internal war, lost land.

sentences.zh: 與木合，國饑。

translations.literal: Meeting wood—state famine.
translations.idiomatic: Meeting wood: famine.

sentences.zh: 水與金合，為變謀，為兵憂。

translations.literal: Water meeting metal—changed plots, army grief.
translations.idiomatic: Water meeting metal: plots and army grief.

sentences.zh: 入太白中而上出，破軍殺將，客勝。

translations.literal: Entering Great White and emerging upward—broken armies, slain generals, guest victory.
translations.idiomatic: Entering White and emerging up: broken armies, guest wins.

sentences.zh: 下出，客亡地，視旗所指，以命破軍。

translations.literal: Emerging downward—guest loses land; read the banner's direction for the broken army.
translations.idiomatic: Emerging down: guest loses land—read the banner.

sentences.zh: 環繞太白，若與鬭，大戰，客勝。

translations.literal: Circling Great White as if battling—great war, guest victory.
translations.idiomatic: Circling White in battle: great war, guest wins.

sentences.zh: 凡木、火、土、金與水鬭，皆為戰，兵不在外，皆為內亂。

translations.literal: Generally wood, fire, earth, metal battling water—all are war; if armies are not outside, all are internal chaos.
translations.idiomatic: Wood, fire, earth, metal battling water—all war or internal chaos.

sentences.zh: 凡同舍為合，相陵為鬭。

translations.literal: Generally same lodge is combination; mutual domination is battle.
translations.idiomatic: Same lodge: combination; domination: battle.

sentences.zh: 二星相近，其殃大，相遠無傷，七寸以內必之。

translations.literal: Two stars close—the calamity is great; far apart no harm; within seven cun must be confirmed.
translations.idiomatic: Close stars: great calamity; within seven cun, confirmed.

sentences.zh: 凡月蝕五星，其國亡。

translations.literal: Generally lunar eclipse of five planets—the state perishes.
translations.idiomatic: Lunar eclipse of five planets: state perishes.

sentences.zh: 歲以饑，熒惑以亂，填以殺，太白以強國戰，辰以女亂。

translations.literal: Year brings famine; Sparkling Fire chaos; Fill killing; Great White strong-state war; Chronogram female chaos.
translations.idiomatic: Year: famine; Fire: chaos; Fill: killing; White: war; Chronogram: female chaos.

sentences.zh: 凡五星入月，其野有逐相。

translations.literal: Generally five planets entering the moon—the field has an expelled chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Five planets entering moon: expelled chancellor.

sentences.zh: 太白，將僇。

translations.literal: Great White—the general is punished.
translations.idiomatic: Great White: general punished.

sentences.zh: 凡五星所聚，其國王，天下從。

translations.literal: Generally where five planets gather—that state's king; the realm follows.
translations.idiomatic: Five planets gathering: that king, realm follows.

sentences.zh: 歲以義從，熒惑以禮從，填以重從，太白以兵從，辰以法，各以其事致天下也。

translations.literal: Year by righteousness; Sparkling Fire by ritual; Fill by weight; Great White by armies; Chronogram by law—each by its affair commands the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Each planet commands the realm by its virtue: righteousness, ritual, weight, armies, law.

sentences.zh: 三星若合，是謂驚立絕行，其國外內有兵，天喪人民，改立侯王。

translations.literal: Three stars if combined—called alarm, standing, severing travel; the state has armies inside and out; Heaven mourns people; marquises and kings are changed.
translations.idiomatic: Three combined: alarm and severed travel—armies, mourning, changed kings.

sentences.zh: 四星若合，是謂太陽，其國兵喪並起，君子憂，小人流。

translations.literal: Four stars combined—called Great Yang; the state has armies and mourning together; gentlemen grieve, petty men flee.
translations.idiomatic: Four combined: Great Yang—armies, mourning, flight.

sentences.zh: 五星若合，是謂易行，有德受慶，改立王者，奄有四方，子孫蕃昌；

translations.literal: Five stars combined—called changing travel; with virtue, blessing; new king established, possessing all four quarters, descendants flourish;
translations.idiomatic: Five combined: changing travel—with virtue, new king and flourishing heirs;

sentences.zh: 亡德受殃，離其國家，滅其宗廟，百姓離去，被滿四方。

translations.literal: without virtue, calamity; state lost, ancestral temple destroyed, people depart, covered across four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: without virtue: lost state, destroyed temple, exiled people.

sentences.zh: 五星皆大，其事亦大；

translations.literal: All five planets large—the affair is also large;
translations.idiomatic: All large: great affair;

sentences.zh: 皆小，事亦小。

translations.literal: all small—the affair is also small.
translations.idiomatic: all small: small affair.

sentences.zh: 凡五星色，其圜白，為喪，為旱；

translations.literal: Generally five planets' color: round white—mourning and drought;
translations.idiomatic: Round white: mourning and drought;

sentences.zh: 赤中不平，為兵，為憂；

translations.literal: red uneven in center—armies and grief;
translations.idiomatic: Red uneven center: armies and grief;

sentences.zh: 青為水；

translations.literal: green—water;
translations.idiomatic: Green: water;

sentences.zh: 黑為疾疫，為多死；

translations.literal: black—pestilence and many deaths;
translations.idiomatic: Black: pestilence and death;

sentences.zh: 黃為吉。

translations.literal: yellow—auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow: auspicious.

sentences.zh: 皆角，赤，犯我城；

translations.literal: All horned: red—enemies attack our walls;
translations.idiomatic: Horned red: enemies at walls;

sentences.zh: 黃，地之爭；

translations.literal: yellow—earthly contention;
translations.idiomatic: Yellow: earthly strife;

sentences.zh: 白，哭泣聲；

translations.literal: white—sound of weeping;
translations.idiomatic: White: weeping;

sentences.zh: 青，有兵憂；

translations.literal: green—army grief;
translations.idiomatic: Green: army grief;

sentences.zh: 黑，有水。

translations.literal: black—water.
translations.idiomatic: Black: water.

sentences.zh: 五星同色，天下偃兵，百姓安寧，歌儛以行，不見災疾，五穀蕃昌。

translations.literal: Five planets same color—armies stilled under Heaven, people secure, song and dance proceed, no disaster or disease, five grains flourish.
translations.idiomatic: Same color: stilled armies, secure people, flourishing grain.

sentences.zh: 凡五星歲政緩則不行，急則過分，逆則占。

translations.literal: Generally Year Star: slow government then no travel; urgent then overstepping; retrograde then take omens.
translations.idiomatic: Year Star slow: no travel; urgent: overstep; retrograde: omens.

sentences.zh: 熒惑，緩則不入，急則不出，違道則占。

translations.literal: Sparkling Fire: slow then no entry; urgent then no exit; against path then omens.
translations.idiomatic: Sparkling Fire slow: no entry; urgent: no exit; against path: omens.

sentences.zh: 填，緩則不還，急則過舍，逆則占。

translations.literal: Fill: slow then no return; urgent then passing lodges; retrograde then omens.
translations.idiomatic: Fill slow: no return; urgent: passing lodges; retrograde: omens.

sentences.zh: 太白，緩則不出，急則不入，逆則占。

translations.literal: Great White: slow then no exit; urgent then no entry; retrograde then omens.
translations.idiomatic: Great White slow: no exit; urgent: no entry; retrograde: omens.

sentences.zh: 辰星，緩則不出，急則不入，非時則占。

translations.literal: Chronogram: slow then no exit; urgent then no entry; wrong season then omens.
translations.idiomatic: Chronogram slow: no exit; urgent: no entry; wrong season: omens.

sentences.zh: 五星不失行，則年谷豐昌。

translations.literal: Five planets not losing their paths—yearly grain flourishes.
translations.idiomatic: Planets on path: flourishing grain.

sentences.zh: 凡五星分天之中，積於東方，中國；

translations.literal: Generally five planets dividing Heaven's center: accumulated in the east—central realm;
translations.idiomatic: Accumulated east: central realm;

sentences.zh: 積於西方，外國。

translations.literal: accumulated in the west—foreign states.
translations.idiomatic: Accumulated west: foreign states.

sentences.zh: 用兵者利。

translations.literal: Those who use armies benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Army users benefit.

sentences.zh: 辰星不出，太白為客；

translations.literal: Chronogram Star not emerging—Great White is guest;
translations.idiomatic: Chronogram not emerging: Great White is guest;

sentences.zh: 其出，太白為主。

translations.literal: when it emerges, Great White is host.
translations.idiomatic: when emerging: Great White is host.

sentences.zh: 出而與太白不相從，及各出一方，為格，野有軍不戰。

translations.literal: Emerging and not following Great White, each emerging from one direction—is called opposition; armies in the wild do not battle.
translations.idiomatic: Not following White from separate directions: opposition—no battle.

sentences.zh: 五星為五德之主，其行或入黃道裡，或出黃道表，猶月行出有陰陽也。

translations.literal: Five planets are masters of the five virtues; their travel may enter inside the Yellow Path or outside—like the moon's yin and yang emergence.
translations.idiomatic: Five planets enter or leave the ecliptic like moon yin-yang.

sentences.zh: 終出入五常，不可以算數求也。

translations.literal: Finally entering and exiting the five constants cannot be sought by calculation.
translations.idiomatic: Five constants' entry and exit cannot be calculated.

sentences.zh: 其東行曰順，西行曰逆，順則疾，逆則遲，通而率之，終為東行矣。

translations.literal: Eastward travel is called direct; westward retrograde; direct is fast, retrograde slow—averaged, it ends as eastward travel.
translations.idiomatic: Eastward is direct and fast; westward retrograde and slow—averaged as eastward.

sentences.zh: 不東不西曰留。

translations.literal: Neither east nor west is called stationary.
translations.idiomatic: Neither east nor west: stationary.

sentences.zh: 與日相近而不見，曰伏。

translations.literal: Near the sun and not seen is called hidden.
translations.idiomatic: Near sun and unseen: hidden.

sentences.zh: 伏與日同度曰合。

translations.literal: Hidden at same degree as sun is called conjunction.
translations.idiomatic: Hidden at sun's degree: conjunction.

sentences.zh: 其留行逆順掩合犯法陵變色芒角，凡其所主，皆以時政五常、五官、五事之得失，而見其變。

translations.literal: Their stationary, direct, retrograde, hidden, combined travel violating law, domination, color change, and horned rays—each governs by seasonal government, five constants, five offices, and five affairs' gain and loss, showing its transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Stationary, direct, retrograde, hidden, combined motion shows government and five affairs' gain and loss.

sentences.zh: 木、火、土三星行遲，夜半經天。

translations.literal: Wood, fire, earth three stars travel slow, crossing heaven at midnight.
translations.idiomatic: Wood, fire, earth travel slow, crossing heaven at midnight.

sentences.zh: 其初皆與日合度，而後順行漸遲，追日不及，晨見東方。

translations.literal: At first all at conjunction with the sun, then direct travel gradually slow, chasing the sun but not reaching, seen at dawn in the east.
translations.idiomatic: At conjunction then direct, gradually slower, seen at eastern dawn.

sentences.zh: 行去日稍遠，朝時近中則留。

translations.literal: Travel departing the sun slightly far, near mid-morning then stationary.
translations.idiomatic: Farther from sun, stationary near mid-morning.

sentences.zh: 留經旦過中則逆行。

translations.literal: Stationary past dawn past mid-heaven then retrograde.
translations.idiomatic: Past dawn mid-heaven: retrograde.

sentences.zh: 逆行至夕時近中則又留。

translations.literal: Retrograde to evening near mid-heaven then again stationary.
translations.idiomatic: Retrograde to evening mid-heaven: again stationary.

sentences.zh: 留而又順，先遲漸速，以至於夕伏西方，乃更與日合。

translations.literal: Stationary then again direct, first slow gradually fast, until evening hiding west, then again conjunction with sun.
translations.idiomatic: Stationary then direct, slow to fast, evening hide west, sun conjunction.

sentences.zh: 金、水二星，行速而不經天。

translations.literal: Metal and water two stars travel fast and do not cross heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Metal and water travel fast without crossing heaven.

sentences.zh: 自始與日合之後，行速而先日，夕見西方。

translations.literal: From first conjunction with sun, travel fast ahead of sun, seen at dusk in west.
translations.idiomatic: After conjunction, fast ahead of sun, seen western dusk.

sentences.zh: 去日前稍遠，夕時欲近南方則漸遲，遲極則留。

translations.literal: Departing sun slightly far, near evening wanting south then gradually slow; at greatest slowness stationary.
translations.idiomatic: Evening southward: gradually slow, then stationary.

sentences.zh: 留而近日，則逆行而合日，在於日後。

translations.literal: Stationary and near sun, then retrograde and conjunction with sun, behind the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Stationary near sun: retrograde conjunction behind sun.

sentences.zh: 晨見東方。

translations.literal: Seen at dawn in east.
translations.idiomatic: Seen eastern dawn.

sentences.zh: 逆極則留，留而後遲。

translations.literal: Retrograde extreme then stationary, stationary then again slow.
translations.idiomatic: Retrograde extreme: stationary, then slow.

sentences.zh: 遲極去日稍遠，旦時欲近南方，則速行以追日，晨伏於東方，複與日合。

translations.literal: Slow extreme departing sun slightly far, near dawn wanting south, then fast travel chasing sun, dawn hiding east, again conjunction with sun.
translations.idiomatic: Slow extreme then fast chase, dawn hide east, sun conjunction.

sentences.zh: 此五星合見、遲速、逆順、留行之大經也。

translations.literal: This is the great principle of five planets' combined appearance, slow-fast, retrograde-direct, and stationary travel.
translations.idiomatic: This is the great principle of five planets' combined, slow, retrograde, and stationary motion.

sentences.zh: 昏旦者，陰陽之大分也。

translations.literal: Dusk and dawn are the great division of yin and yang.
translations.idiomatic: Dusk and dawn divide yin and yang.

sentences.zh: 南方者，太陽之位，而天地之經也。

translations.literal: The south is Great Yang's position and Heaven-Earth's meridian.
translations.idiomatic: South is Great Yang's position and the meridian.

sentences.zh: 七曜行至陽位，當天之經，則虧昃留逆而不居焉。

translations.literal: The seven luminaries traveling to the yang position, at Heaven's meridian, then wane, slant, stay, retrograde and do not dwell.
translations.idiomatic: Seven luminaries at yang meridian wane, slant, stay, retrograde.

sentences.zh: 此天之常道也。

translations.literal: This is Heaven's constant Way.
translations.idiomatic: This is Heaven's constant Way.

sentences.zh: 三星經天，二星不經天，三天兩地之道也。

translations.literal: Three stars cross heaven; two do not—three heavens two earths' Way.
translations.idiomatic: Three cross heaven; two do not—three heavens, two earths.

sentences.zh: 凡五星見伏留行，逆順遲速，應曆度者，為得其行，政合于常。

translations.literal: Generally five planets' appearance, hiding, stationary travel, retrograde-direct, slow-fast responding to calendrical degrees—obtaining their paths, government harmonizes with the constant.
translations.idiomatic: Planets responding to degrees obtain their paths—government in harmony.

sentences.zh: 違曆錯度，而失路盈縮者，為亂行。

translations.literal: Violating calendar, missing degrees, losing path, expanding and contracting—disordered travel.
translations.idiomatic: Violating calendar and degrees: disordered travel.

sentences.zh: 亂行則為妖星彗孛，而有亡國革政，兵饑喪亂之禍云。

translations.literal: Disordered travel becomes baleful stars, comets, and brooms—with fallen states, changed government, armies, famine, mourning, and chaos.
translations.idiomatic: Disordered travel becomes comets and brooms—ruin, war, famine, chaos.

sentences.zh: 古曆五星並順行，秦曆始有金火之逆。

translations.literal: Ancient calendars had all five planets direct; Qin calendar first had metal and fire retrograde.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient calendars: all direct; Qin first had metal and fire retrograde.

sentences.zh: 又甘、石並時，自有差異。

translations.literal: Also Gan and Shi were contemporaries yet had their own differences.
translations.idiomatic: Gan and Shi were contemporaries yet differed.

sentences.zh: 漢初測候，乃知五星皆有逆行，其後相承罕能察。

translations.literal: At Han's beginning through observation, it was known all five planets have retrograde motion; afterward transmitters rarely could discern it.
translations.idiomatic: Han observers learned all five planets retrograde; later transmitters rarely discerned it.

sentences.zh: 至後魏末，清河張子信，學藝博通，尤精歷數。

translations.literal: By late Northern Wei, Zhang Zixin of Qinghe, learning broad and penetrating, especially refined in calendrical reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Late Northern Wei: Zhang Zixin of Qinghe, master of calendrical reckoning.

sentences.zh: 因避葛榮亂，隱於海島中，積三十許年，專以渾儀測候日月五星差變之數，以算步之，始悟日月交道，有表裡遲速，五星見伏，有感召向背。

translations.literal: Avoiding Ge Rong's chaos, he hid on an island thirty-odd years, exclusively using the armillary sphere to observe sun, moon, and five planets' differential numbers, calculating and stepping them—first comprehending sun-moon crossing paths have inner-outer slow-fast, and five planets' appearance and hiding have sympathetic facing and backing.
translations.idiomatic: Hiding on an island thirty years with an armillary sphere, Zhang Zixin grasped eclipse paths and planetary appearance.

sentences.zh: 言日行在春分後則遲，秋分後則速。

translations.literal: He said the sun's daily travel is slow after spring equinox and fast after autumn equinox.
translations.idiomatic: Sun travel is slow after spring equinox, fast after autumn equinox.

sentences.zh: 合朔月在日道裡則日食，若在日道外，雖交不虧。

translations.literal: At conjunction if the moon is inside the sun's path there is solar eclipse; if outside the sun's path, though crossing, no loss.
translations.idiomatic: Moon inside sun's path at conjunction: eclipse; outside: no loss though crossing.

sentences.zh: 月望值交則虧，不問表裡。

translations.literal: At full moon meeting crossing there is loss, regardless of inner or outer.
translations.idiomatic: Full moon at crossing always eclipses, inner or outer.

sentences.zh: 又月行遇木、火、土、金四星，向之則速，背之則遲。

translations.literal: Also moon travel meeting wood, fire, earth, metal four stars—facing them is fast, backing them is slow.
translations.idiomatic: Moon facing four planets is fast; backing them, slow.

sentences.zh: 五星行四方列宿，各有所好惡。

translations.literal: Five planets traveling the four quarters' lodges each have what they favor and hate.
translations.idiomatic: Five planets in lodges each favor and hate certain places.

sentences.zh: 所居遇其好者，則留多行遲，見早。

translations.literal: Where they dwell meeting what they favor—then long stationary, slow travel, early appearance.
translations.idiomatic: Favored lodges: long stationary, slow travel, early appearance.

sentences.zh: 遇其惡者，則留少行速，見遲。

translations.literal: Meeting what they hate—then short stationary, fast travel, late appearance.
translations.idiomatic: Hated lodges: short stationary, fast travel, late appearance.

sentences.zh: 與常數並差，少者差至五度，多者差至三十許度。

translations.literal: Differing from constant numbers—lesser difference to five degrees, greater to thirty-odd degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Differences from constants: up to five or thirty degrees.

sentences.zh: 其辰星之行，見伏尤異。

translations.literal: Chronogram Star's travel—appearance and hiding are especially anomalous.
translations.idiomatic: Chronogram Star's appearance and hiding are especially anomalous.

sentences.zh: 晨應見在雨水後立夏前，夕應見在處暑後霜降前者，並不見。

translations.literal: Should appear at dawn after Rain Water before Start of Summer; should appear at dusk after End of Heat before Frost's Descent—both not seen.
translations.idiomatic: Expected dawn and dusk appearances often not seen.

sentences.zh: 啟蟄、立夏、立秋、霜降四氣之內，晨夕去日前後三十六度內，十八度外，有木、火、土、金一星者見，無者不見。

translations.literal: Within Awakening, Start of Summer, Start of Autumn, Frost's Descent four qi—dawn and dusk within thirty-six degrees before and after the sun, eighteen degrees outside, if wood-fire-earth-metal one star appears it is seen; if none, not seen.
translations.idiomatic: Within four seasonal nodes, planets within certain solar degrees appear or not.

sentences.zh: 後張胄玄、劉孝孫、劉焯等，依此差度，為定入交食分及五星定見定行，與天密會，皆古人所未得也。

translations.literal: Later Zhang Zhouxuan, Liu Xiaosun, Liu Chao and others, following these differential degrees, fixed eclipse fractions and five planets' fixed appearance and fixed travel—matching Heaven closely—all never obtained by ancients.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhouxuan, Liu Xiaosun, and Liu Chao fixed eclipses and planetary motion—unmatched by ancients.

sentences.zh: 梁奉朝請祖暅，天監中，受詔集古天官及圖緯舊說，撰《天文錄》三十卷。

translations.literal: Liang court gentleman Zu Geng, during Tianjian, received edict to gather ancient star officials and weft-text old theories, compiling Astronomy Record in thirty volumes.
translations.idiomatic: Liang's Zu Geng compiled the thirty-volume Astronomy Record under Tianjian.

sentences.zh: 逮周氏克梁，獲庾季才，為太史令，撰《靈台秘苑》一百二十卷，占驗益備。

translations.literal: When Zhou conquered Liang, they obtained Yu Jicai as Grand Astrologer, compiling Secret Canon of the Spirit Tower in one hundred twenty volumes—divination and verification more complete.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou obtained Yu Jicai, who compiled the Secret Canon of the Spirit Tower in 120 volumes.

sentences.zh: 今略其雜星、瑞星、妖星、客星、流星及雲氣名狀，次之於此云。

translations.literal: Now briefly the miscellaneous stars, auspicious stars, baleful stars, guest stars, shooting stars, and cloud-qi names and forms are placed hereafter.
translations.idiomatic: Below are miscellaneous, auspicious, baleful, guest, and shooting stars and cloud forms.

sentences.zh: 瑞星一曰景星，如半月，生於晦朔，助月為明。

translations.literal: Auspicious star one is called Luminous Star—like a half moon, born at new and full moon, assisting the moon as brightness.
translations.idiomatic: Auspicious star one: Luminous Star, half-moon at new and full moon.

sentences.zh: 或曰，星大而中空。

translations.literal: Or: star large and hollow in center.
translations.idiomatic: Or: large star hollow at center.

sentences.zh: 或曰，有三星，在赤方氣，與青方氣相連。

translations.literal: Or: three stars in red方 qi connected to green方 qi.
translations.idiomatic: Or: three stars in red qi connected to green qi.

sentences.zh: 黃星在赤方氣中，亦名德星。

translations.literal: Yellow star in red方 qi—also called Virtue Star.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow star in red qi is also Virtue Star.

sentences.zh: 二曰周伯星，黃色煌煌然，所見之國大昌。

translations.literal: Two is Zhou Bo Star—yellow and brilliant; the state where seen greatly flourishes.
translations.idiomatic: Two: Zhou Bo Star—yellow and brilliant; seen state flourishes.

sentences.zh: 三曰含譽，光耀似彗，喜則含譽射。

translations.literal: Three is Containing Praise—light like a comet; when pleased, Containing Praise shoots.
translations.idiomatic: Three: Containing Praise—comet-like light when pleased.

sentences.zh: 星雜變一曰星晝見。

translations.literal: Star miscellaneous change one is stars seen by day.
translations.idiomatic: Miscellaneous change one: stars seen by day.

sentences.zh: 若星與日並出，名曰嫁女。

translations.literal: If star and sun appear together, called Marrying Daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Star and sun together: Marrying Daughter.

sentences.zh: 星與日爭光，武且弱，文且強，女子為王，在邑為喪，在野為兵。

translations.literal: Star contending light with sun—military weakens, civil strengthens, woman becomes king; in city mourning, in field armies.
translations.idiomatic: Star-sun light rivalry: weak military, strong civil, woman king.

sentences.zh: 又曰，臣有奸心，上不明，臣下從橫，大水浩洋。

translations.literal: Also: ministers have treacherous hearts, lord not enlightened, subordinates unrestrained, great flood vast.
translations.idiomatic: Also: treacherous ministers, dark lord, vast flood.

sentences.zh: 又曰，星晝見，虹不滅，臣人生明，星奪日光，天下有立王。

translations.literal: Also: stars by day, rainbow not extinguished, subjects give light, star seizes sun's light—a king is established under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Also: day stars and enduring rainbow mean a new king.

sentences.zh: 二曰恆星不見。

translations.literal: Two is fixed stars not seen.
translations.idiomatic: Two: fixed stars not seen.

sentences.zh: 恆星者，在位人君之類。

translations.literal: Fixed stars are the class of lords in office.
translations.idiomatic: Fixed stars are lords in office.

sentences.zh: 不見者，象諸侯之背畔，不佐王者奉順法度，無君之象也。

translations.literal: Not seen means image of feudal lords turning against, not assisting the king in following law, no lord's image.
translations.idiomatic: Not seen: lords rebel, no lord's image.

sentences.zh: 又曰，恆星不見，主不嚴，法度消。

translations.literal: Also: fixed stars not seen—the lord is not strict, law dissolves.
translations.idiomatic: Also: lord not strict, law dissolves.

sentences.zh: 又曰，天子失政，諸侯橫暴。

translations.literal: Also: Son of Heaven loses government, feudal lords are violent.
translations.idiomatic: Also: lost government, violent lords.

sentences.zh: 又曰，常星列宿不見，象中國諸侯微滅也。

translations.literal: Also: constant stars and lodges not seen—image of central realm's feudal lords fading and perishing.
translations.idiomatic: Also: unseen lodges mean fading lords.

sentences.zh: 三曰星斗，星斗天下大亂。

translations.literal: Three is stars battling—stars battling means great chaos under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Three: stars battling—great chaos.

sentences.zh: 四曰星搖，星搖人眾將勞。

translations.literal: Four is stars trembling—stars trembling, multitudes will toil.
translations.idiomatic: Four: trembling stars—people toil.

sentences.zh: 五曰星隕。

translations.literal: Five is stars falling.
translations.idiomatic: Five: stars falling.

sentences.zh: 大星隕下，陽失其位，災害之萌也。

translations.literal: Great stars falling—yang loses its position, the bud of disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Great stars falling: yang loses position—disaster buds.

sentences.zh: 又曰，眾星墜，人失其所也。

translations.literal: Also: many stars fall—people lose their place.
translations.idiomatic: Also: many falling stars—people lose place.

sentences.zh: 凡星所墜，國易政。

translations.literal: Generally stars that fall—the state changes government.
translations.idiomatic: Falling stars: changed government.

sentences.zh: 又曰，星墜，當其下有戰場，天下亂，期三年。

translations.literal: Also: stars fall—below is a battlefield; realm chaos, term three years.
translations.idiomatic: Also: battlefield below, three-year chaos.

sentences.zh: 又曰，奔星之所墜，其下有兵，列宿之所墜，滅家邦，眾星之所墜，眾庶亡。

translations.literal: Also: where shooting stars fall, armies below; where lodges fall, families and states destroyed; where many stars fall, multitudes perish.
translations.idiomatic: Shooting stars: armies; lodges: destroyed states; many stars: dead multitudes.

sentences.zh: 又曰，填星墜，海水泆，黃星騁，海水躍。

translations.literal: Also: Fill Star falls—seawater overflows; yellow star gallops—seawater leaps.
translations.idiomatic: Fill falling: seawater overflows; yellow star: seawater leaps.

sentences.zh: 又曰，黃星墜，海水傾。

translations.literal: Also: yellow star falls—seawater topples.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow star falling: seawater topples.

sentences.zh: 亦曰，星墜而渤海決。

translations.literal: Also: stars fall and Bohai breaks open.
translations.idiomatic: Stars fall and Bohai breaks.

sentences.zh: 星隕如雨，天子微，諸侯力政，五伯代興，更為盟主，眾暴寡，大並小。

translations.literal: Stars falling like rain—Son of Heaven weak, feudal lords forceful government, Five Hegemons rise in turn as covenant lords, many overpower few, great swallow small.
translations.idiomatic: Star-rain: weak Son of Heaven, hegemon struggle.

sentences.zh: 又曰，星辰附離天，猶庶人附離王者也。

translations.literal: Also: stars attached departing heaven—like multitudes departing kings.
translations.idiomatic: Stars leaving heaven: like people leaving kings.

sentences.zh: 王者失道，綱紀廢，下將畔去。

translations.literal: King loses the Way, statutes abolished, subordinates will rebel and depart.
translations.idiomatic: King loses Way, statutes abolished, rebellion.

sentences.zh: 故星畔天而隕，以見其象。

translations.literal: Therefore stars rebel against heaven and fall—to show the image.
translations.idiomatic: Stars rebel against heaven and fall—showing the image.

sentences.zh: 國有兵凶，則星墜為鳥獸。

translations.literal: State has armies and calamity—stars fall as birds and beasts.
translations.idiomatic: Armies and calamity: stars fall as beasts.

sentences.zh: 天下將亡，則星墜為飛蟲。

translations.literal: Realm about to perish—stars fall as flying insects.
translations.idiomatic: Realm perishing: stars fall as insects.

sentences.zh: 天下大兵，則星墜為金鐵。

translations.literal: Great armies under Heaven—stars fall as metal and iron.
translations.idiomatic: Great armies: stars fall as metal.

sentences.zh: 天下有水，則星墜為土。

translations.literal: Flood under Heaven—stars fall as earth.
translations.idiomatic: Flood: stars fall as earth.

sentences.zh: 國主亡，有兵，則星墜為草木。

translations.literal: State lord perishes, armies—stars fall as grass and trees.
translations.idiomatic: Dead lord and armies: stars fall as plants.

sentences.zh: 兵起，國主亡，則星墜為沙。

translations.literal: Armies rise, state lord perishes—stars fall as sand.
translations.idiomatic: Armies and dead lord: stars fall as sand.

sentences.zh: 星墜，為人而言者，善惡如其言。

translations.literal: Stars falling as speaking humans—good and evil as their speech.
translations.idiomatic: Falling speakers: good and evil as spoken.

sentences.zh: 又曰，國有大喪，則星墜為龍。

translations.literal: Also: state has great mourning—stars fall as dragons.
translations.idiomatic: Great mourning: stars fall as dragons.

sentences.zh: 妖星妖星者，五行之氣，五星之變名，見其方，以為殃災。

translations.literal: Baleful stars are the names of five phases' qi and five stars' transformations; seen in their direction, taken as calamity and disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Baleful stars are five phases' and five stars' transformations—calamity by direction.

sentences.zh: 各以其日五色占，知何國吉凶決矣。

translations.literal: Each by its day's five colors take omens, knowing which state's fortune and misfortune is decided.
translations.idiomatic: By day and five colors, each state's fortune is decided.

sentences.zh: 行見無道之國，失禮之邦，為兵為饑，水旱死亡之征也。

translations.literal: Appearing and traveling in states without the Way, states losing ritual—armies, famine, flood, drought, death omens.
translations.idiomatic: In lawless states: armies, famine, flood, drought, death.

sentences.zh: 又曰，凡妖星所出，形狀不同，為殃如一。

translations.literal: Also: generally baleful stars emerging differ in shape but calamity is the same.
translations.idiomatic: Baleful stars differ in shape; calamity is the same.

sentences.zh: 其出不過一年，若三年，必有破國屠城。

translations.literal: Emergence not exceeding one year, or three years—certainly broken state, slaughtered city.
translations.idiomatic: Emergence within one to three years: broken state, slaughtered city.

sentences.zh: 其君死，天下大亂，兵士亂行，戰死於野，積屍從橫。

translations.literal: Its lord dies, great chaos under Heaven, soldiers disorderly travel, battle death in the wild, corpses piled crosswise.
translations.idiomatic: Lord dies, chaos, corpses piled crosswise.

sentences.zh: 余殃不盡，為水旱兵饑疾疫之殃。

translations.literal: Remaining calamity not exhausted—water, drought, armies, famine, pestilence calamities.
translations.idiomatic: Remaining calamity: flood, drought, war, famine, plague.

sentences.zh: 又曰，凡妖星出見，長大，災深期遠；

translations.literal: Also: generally when baleful stars appear and are large and long—calamity deep, term far;
translations.idiomatic: Large baleful stars: deep calamity, far term;

sentences.zh: 短小，災淺期近。

translations.literal: small and short—calamity shallow, term near.
translations.idiomatic: Small: shallow calamity, near term.

sentences.zh: 三尺至五尺，期百日。

translations.literal: Three to five chi—term one hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: Three to five chi: one hundred days.

sentences.zh: 五尺至一丈，期一年。

translations.literal: Five chi to one zhang—term one year.
translations.idiomatic: Five chi to one zhang: one year.

sentences.zh: 一丈至三丈，期三年。

translations.literal: One zhang to three zhang—term three years.
translations.idiomatic: One to three zhang: three years.

sentences.zh: 三丈至五丈，期五年。

translations.literal: Three to five zhang—term five years.
translations.idiomatic: Three to five zhang: five years.

sentences.zh: 五丈至十丈，期七年。

translations.literal: Five to ten zhang—term seven years.
translations.idiomatic: Five to ten zhang: seven years.

sentences.zh: 十丈以上，期九年。

translations.literal: Above ten zhang—term nine years.
translations.idiomatic: Above ten zhang: nine years.

sentences.zh: 審以察之，其災必應。

translations.literal: Examined carefully—the calamity certainly responds.
translations.idiomatic: Careful examination: calamity responds.

sentences.zh: 彗星，世所謂掃星，本類星，末類彗，小者數寸，長或竟天。

translations.literal: Comets—what the world calls broom stars—originally like stars, finally like comets; small ones several cun, long ones spanning heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Comets, broom stars—star-like at head, comet-like at tail; small to heaven-spanning.

sentences.zh: 見則兵起，大水。

translations.literal: Appearance means armies rise, great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Appearance: armies and great flood.

sentences.zh: 主掃除，除舊佈新。

translations.literal: Governing sweeping away—removing old and spreading new.
translations.idiomatic: Governing sweeping—removing old, spreading new.

sentences.zh: 有五色，各依五行本精所主。

translations.literal: Have five colors, each according to five phases' native essences governed.
translations.idiomatic: Five colors by five phases' essences.

sentences.zh: 史臣案，彗體無光，傅日而為光，故夕見則東指，晨見則西指，在日南北，皆隨日光而指。

translations.literal: The Record Officer notes: comet bodies have no light; attached to the sun they have light—therefore seen at dusk pointing east, at dawn pointing west; north or south of the sun, all follow sunlight in pointing.
translations.idiomatic: Comets borrow sunlight—dusk east, dawn west.

sentences.zh: 頓挫其芒，或長或短，光芒所及則為災。

translations.literal: Halting and breaking their rays, sometimes long sometimes short—where rays reach is calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Halting rays, long or short—calamity where rays reach.

sentences.zh: 又曰，孛星，彗之屬也。

translations.literal: Also: Broom Star, comet category.
translations.idiomatic: Also: Broom Star, comet category.

sentences.zh: 偏指曰彗，芒氣四出曰孛。

translations.literal: Pointing obliquely is comet; ray qi spreading four directions is broom.
translations.idiomatic: Oblique pointing: comet; rays four directions: broom.

sentences.zh: 孛者，孛然非常，惡氣之所生也。

translations.literal: Broom means broom-like anomaly—born of wicked qi.
translations.idiomatic: Broom: anomalous wicked qi.

sentences.zh: 內不有大亂，則外有大兵，天下合謀，暗蔽不明，有所傷害。

translations.literal: If not great internal chaos, then great external armies; realm conspires together, dark and obscured, harm occurs.
translations.idiomatic: Without internal chaos, external armies; conspiracy and harm.

sentences.zh: 晏子曰：「君若不改，孛星將出，彗星何懼乎？

translations.literal: Master Yan said: "If the lord does not reform, the broom star will emerge—why fear comets?"
translations.idiomatic: Master Yan: "Without reform, broom star emerges—why fear comets?"

sentences.zh: 」由是言之，災甚於彗。

translations.literal: From this speaking—calamity exceeds comets.
translations.idiomatic: Thus broom calamity exceeds comets.

sentences.zh: 歲星之精，流為天棓、天槍、天猾、天衝、國皇、反登。

translations.literal: Year Star's essence flows into Celestial Pestle, Celestial Spear, Celestial Mischief, Celestial Rush, State Sovereign, Reverse Ascent.
translations.idiomatic: Year Star's essence: Pestle, Spear, Mischief, Rush, State Sovereign, Reverse Ascent.

sentences.zh: 一曰天棓，一名覺星，或曰天格。

translations.literal: One is Celestial Pestle—also called Awakening Star, or Celestial Frame.
translations.idiomatic: One: Celestial Pestle—Awakening Star or Celestial Frame.

sentences.zh: 本類星，末銳，長四丈。

translations.literal: Originally star-like, finally sharp, four zhang long.
translations.idiomatic: Star-like head, sharp tail, four zhang.

sentences.zh: 主滅兵，主奮爭。

translations.literal: Governing destroying armies, governing fierce contention.
translations.idiomatic: Destroying armies, fierce contention.

sentences.zh: 又曰，天棓出，其國凶，不可舉事用兵。

translations.literal: Also: Celestial Pestle emerging—that state is inauspicious; do not raise armies.
translations.idiomatic: Pestle emerging: inauspicious state—no armies.

sentences.zh: 又曰，期三月，必有破軍拔城。

translations.literal: Also: term three months—certainly broken army and captured city.
translations.idiomatic: Three months: broken army, captured city.

sentences.zh: 又曰，天棓見，女主用事。

translations.literal: Also: Celestial Pestle seen—queen consort holds affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Pestle seen: queen holds affairs.

sentences.zh: 其本者為主人。

translations.literal: Its root is the master.
translations.idiomatic: Its root is the master.

sentences.zh: 二曰天槍，主捕制。

translations.literal: Two is Celestial Spear, governing capture and restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Two: Celestial Spear—capture and restraint.

sentences.zh: 或曰，攙云如牛，槍云如馬。

translations.literal: Or: Coiling Cloud like ox, Spear Cloud like horse.
translations.idiomatic: Or: Coiling Cloud like ox, Spear Cloud like horse.

sentences.zh: 或曰，如槍，左右銳，長數丈。

translations.literal: Or: like spear, left and right sharp, several zhang long.
translations.idiomatic: Or: spear-like, sharp left and right, several zhang.

sentences.zh: 天攙本類星，未銳，長丈。

translations.literal: Celestial Coiling originally star-like, finally sharp, one zhang long.
translations.idiomatic: Celestial Coiling: star head, sharp tail, one zhang.

sentences.zh: 三曰天猾，主招亂。

translations.literal: Three is Celestial Mischief, governing summoning chaos.
translations.idiomatic: Three: Celestial Mischief—summoning chaos.

sentences.zh: 又曰，人主自恣，逆天暴物，則天猾起。

translations.literal: Also: human lord self-indulgent, violating Heaven and violently treating things—Celestial Mischief rises.
translations.idiomatic: Self-indulgent lord violating Heaven: Celestial Mischief rises.

sentences.zh: 四曰天衝，狀如人，蒼衣赤首，不動。

translations.literal: Four is Celestial Rush—shaped like a person, dark robes and red head, unmoving.
translations.idiomatic: Four: Celestial Rush—human-shaped, dark robes, red head, unmoving.

sentences.zh: 主滅位。

translations.literal: Governing destroying position.
translations.idiomatic: Destroying position.

sentences.zh: 又曰，衝星出，臣謀主，武卒發。

translations.literal: Also: Rush Star emerging—ministers plot against lord, martial soldiers rise.
translations.idiomatic: Rush emerging: ministers plot, soldiers rise.

sentences.zh: 又曰，天衝抱極泣帝前，血濁霧下，天下冤。

translations.literal: Also: Celestial Rush embraces the pole weeping before the Emperor—blood turbid mist descends, injustice under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Rush at pole weeping before Emperor: blood mist, universal injustice.

sentences.zh: 五曰國皇。

translations.literal: Five is State Sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Five: State Sovereign.

sentences.zh: 或曰，機星散為國皇。

translations.literal: Or: Pivot Star scatters into State Sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Or: Pivot Star scatters into State Sovereign.

sentences.zh: 國皇之星，大而赤，類南極老人星也。

translations.literal: State Sovereign star, large and red, like South Pole Old Man Star.
translations.idiomatic: State Sovereign: large red, like South Pole Old Man.

sentences.zh: 主滅奸，主內寇難。

translations.literal: Governing destroying wickedness, governing internal bandit calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Destroying wickedness, internal bandit calamity.

sentences.zh: 見則兵起，天下急。

translations.literal: Seen—armies rise, realm urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Seen: armies, urgent realm.

sentences.zh: 或云，去地一二丈，如炬火狀。

translations.literal: Or: one or two zhang from earth, like torch fire.
translations.idiomatic: Or: one-two zhang from earth like torch.

sentences.zh: 後客星內亦有國皇，名同而占狀異。

translations.literal: Later among guest stars there is also State Sovereign—same name, different omen form.
translations.idiomatic: Later guest stars also have State Sovereign—same name, different omens.

sentences.zh: 六曰反登，主夷分，皆少陽之精，司徒之類，青龍七宿之域。

translations.literal: Six is Reverse Ascent, governing barbarian division—all lesser yang essence, Minister of Public Works class, azure dragon seven lodges' domain.
translations.idiomatic: Six: Reverse Ascent, barbarian division—lesser yang, Public Works, azure dragon domain.

sentences.zh: 有謀反，若恣虐為害，主失春政者，以出時衝為期。

translations.literal: If plotting rebellion or wanton cruelty as harm, lord losing spring government—emergence time as term.
